reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides a step-by-step explanation of affiliate marketing, including referral links, commissions, and instructional earnings examples. Its commercial referral relationships are disclosed, and the material explicitly has no paid course or sales pitch. The referral links and commission examples are presented as instruction rather than guaranteed returns or requests to transfer money.

We get custom links from those business that tracks when people click on our link and goes to that business and then if that person buys from that business, we then get a commission
DISCLAIMER: This video and description contains affiliate links, which means that if you click on one of the product links, I’ll receive a small commission.
this is basically how you can create a website really easily through WordPress
You don't need to pay any money to learn how to do this. This is totally free.

opening.argument: The video links income to concrete actions rather than merely describing a business concept. It explains that an affiliate receives money after someone clicks a special link and buys, while directing viewers toward building a website through a linked provider. The description separately confirms that clicks on listed product links generate commissions for the speaker. That creates a clear action-to-payment solicitation: viewers are encouraged to set up the infrastructure and drive clicks or purchases through tracked links in order to obtain income. The low-entry framing makes the proposed earning path appear unusually accessible, even though the payment depends on successful conversions.

citations.quote: when somebody clicks on that and then they buy something through that link that they have clicked on, I then will get a commission
if you find value in this video we would appreciate if you built a website using that link
if you click on one of the product links, I’ll receive a small commission
let's go ahead and let's go through with purchasing this plan

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a tutorial does not remove the solicitation. The explanation of tracked clicks and purchases is precisely the mechanism by which participants are expected to earn, and the presentation moves from that mechanism to purchasing hosting and using a linked provider. Saying there is no paid course addresses only one possible payment request; it does not address the promoted affiliate pathway or the promised commission relationship.

citations.quote: we are promoting products for other businesses and in return for promoting those products we are getting some of the commission
we're partnered with them. It's actually an affiliate link
You don't need to pay any money to learn how to do this. This is totally free

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited mechanics show ordinary affiliate compensation, not a guaranteed reward for the viewer. The commission is described as contingent on another person buying after clicking, and the linked hosting purchase is optional. The opening also omits the video's explicit statement that viewers do not have to pay for a course, so the evidence does not establish that the video promises effortless payment to participants.

citations.quote: if that person buys from that business, we then get a commission or a piece of the pie from that company
I made about five thousand three hundred dollars in affiliate Commission's in profit in my pocket
don't feel the pressure, too. You don't have to

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: the speaker presents affiliate marketing as startable for zero dollars, gives a concrete example of $202 from 100 clicks, and displays commission rates and earnings-per-click information. The video also routes viewers to external commercial links, including hosting and website services, while the speaker acknowledges a partnership. Although results are described as variable, the use of specific dollar figures and the repeated emphasis on inexpensive entry can make the opportunity look like a simple, low-risk income system. A careful judge should treat that combination as promotional financial persuasion rather than assume that a disclaimer neutralizes the earnings appeal.

citations.quote: with affiliate marketing there does not need to be any startup cost
for a hundred clicks they might end up getting 202 dollars in total
we're partnered with them. It's actually an affiliate link

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes disclosure and the absence of a course, but neither resolves the unusually easy-entry and earnings framing. The video still supplies specific return figures, promotes a website-building route, and uses an affiliate relationship to monetize that route. A warning that outcomes vary does not undo the persuasive effect of presenting $202 from 100 clicks or thousands of dollars in commissions.

citations.quote: they might end up getting 202 dollars in total
last month I made about five thousand three hundred dollars in affiliate Commission's in profit in my pocket
you can get started with this for $0

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are examples and operational metrics, not fixed returns. The same material says results depend on the audience and that promoting the offer to people without money may not produce many conversions. It also explains that paid traffic costs money and that the speaker's own links are disclosed. Specific examples therefore do not establish deception or a guaranteed low-risk payout.

citations.quote: It obviously varies depending on the type of traffic that you are getting to

opening.argument: The educational wrapper also functions as a promotion funnel. The video begins as a beginner tutorial, then directs viewers toward a specific hosting company, demonstrates purchasing a hosting plan, and offers another website provider with a discount code. The speaker explicitly says the hosting link is an affiliate link and asks viewers who found value to use it. That commercial steering is central to the practical pathway being taught: viewers are not just learning how affiliate marketing works, but are being guided toward a monetized setup and external services. The instructional format therefore makes the solicitation appear like neutral operational help.

citations.quote: we're partnered with them. It's actually an affiliate link
this cost me $47 to have a website for two years
if you use the code Santral Media you can get 10% off
Create an affiliate marketing website: https://santrelmedia.com/Hostinger

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the video teaches website construction does not make the commercial steering incidental. It names providers, shows a hosting purchase, and supplies a discount code while acknowledging that the speaker benefits from the link. A tutorial can still be the vehicle for soliciting purchases and downstream affiliate activity, so the educational label does not settle the character of the presentation.

citations.quote: let's go ahead and let's go through with purchasing this plan
you can build a website through that and if you use the code Santral Media you can get 10% off
we would appreciate if you built a website using that link

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The commercial references are openly identified as affiliate links, and the video does not hide that the speaker may receive a commission. Demonstrating a website setup and mentioning an optional discount are consistent with operational instruction. The cited material does not show coercion, a required purchase, or a promised return to viewers; it shows disclosed promotion alongside education.
